title: Translation Agency config
description: Schema for translation.config.json — the per-project settings file for the Translation Agency toolkit. Lives at the root of the project being translated (not in the toolkit folder). All fields are optional; command-line flags override the file for a single run. See CLAUDE.md and README.md 'Configuration'.

$schema.description: Pointer to this JSON Schema, giving editors autocomplete and validation. Keep it as the raw GitHub URL so it resolves from any project the file is copied into.

sourceLang.description: Language code of the source files (the language you are translating FROM), e.g. 'en'. If omitted, the skill detects it.

targetLangs.description: Language codes to translate INTO, e.g. ['de', 'fr', 'es']. Locale forms like 'pt-BR' or 'de_DE' are fine.

specialization.description: The domain profile(s) the translator panel loads for terminology and framing. Either a single module name (string) or, to LAYER domains, an array of names — the first is primary (it wins tone/framing conflicts), and every layer contributes its terminology + verbatim rules. Built-ins: general (default) | technical | marketing | legal | finance | medical | ecommerce | travel | government | scientific. Not enum-restricted — a custom specializations/<name>.md module is also a valid value. Override per run with /translate --domain <name> (or --domain a,b to layer).

glossary.description: Optional path to a project glossary CSV (source,lang,term,context,confidence,source,notes). Overrides the specialization on any term it defines; the research pass writes/updates this file.

context.description: What this project IS — purpose, audience, register/brand voice, domain notes. Lets the translator pick the right sense of a word. A short description inline, OR a path to a translation-context.md file.

formality.description: Register / T–V distinction the panel enforces where a language has one (German du/Sie, French tu/vous, Spanish tú/usted, Japanese politeness). Either a single string applied to every target language, or an object for per-language control ({ "default": …, "de": …, "ja": … }) whose values are the same enum; unlisted languages fall back to 'default', else 'auto'. 'auto' (also the meaning when the field is absent) uses the language's conventional register for this product/context — today's behavior, non-breaking. Where a language has no T–V distinction, formal/informal is read as overall tone. Resolution (later wins): --formality flag → this setting → auto.

oneOf.description: One register applied to every target language.
Per-language register. Optional 'default' key plus any BCP-47/locale keys (e.g. 'de', 'pt-BR', 'ja'); each value is formal|informal|auto. Unlisted languages fall back to 'default', else 'auto'.

doNotTranslate.description: Manual pass-through / verbatim rules — one plain-language instruction per item for strings that look like copy but are project-specific data and must stay byte-identical. The panel treats each as absolute and adds covered values to the C1/C3 verbatim exempt list. Use for patterns/categories; for a single fixed term prefer a glossary row with lang=*.

research.description: Terminology-research pass (translate-researcher) that builds a per-language glossary before translating. 'first-run' (default) researches once per project/language then reuses the glossary; 'always' re-researches every run; 'off' never runs it. Force a refresh any run with --research.

queries.description: How uncertain strings are handled. 'report' (default) best-guesses and logs each uncertainty to projects/<slug>/queries-<date>.md without interrupting you; 'high-stakes' also asks interactively for a few legal/medical/financial terms; 'off' best-guesses and writes no queries file.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project/files to translate (e.g. C:/Users/you/Projects/MyApp). Empty = the current directory. Override per run with /translate --path <path>.

include.description: Glob list of translatable files, relative to projectPath (e.g. ['src/i18n/**', 'content/**']).

exclude.description: Glob list of files to skip, relative to projectPath (e.g. ['**/node_modules/**', 'translations/**']).

mode.description: 'inplace' (default) writes each translation as a sibling next to its source, swapping/appending the language code; 'tree' copies every file into <projectPath>/<dir>/<lang>/ and translates the copies; 'catalog' edits existing per-language files in place (messages.<lang>.ts, de.json, .po).

dir.description: Output directory name used by 'tree' mode only (default 'translations').

verifyCmd.description: Cheap per-batch check (type/lint) run after each batch. Leave empty for plain document sets.

buildCmd.description: Build/verify command run once at the end of the run. Leave empty for plain document sets.

creditInCommit.description: Optional attribution in git history. Default false. When true, and only when the run actually commits (inplace/catalog mode in a git repo), the translation commit gets a 'Translated-with: Translation Agency <version> (<repo URL>)' trailer — nothing is ever written into the translated files. The run report always credits the tool regardless.

makeJson.description: Compile the Jed-format WP JSON artifacts from the translated .po files (needs WP-CLI or gettext tools). Default false.

makeMo.description: Compile .mo artifacts from the translated .po files (needs WP-CLI or gettext tools). Default false.

^\\$comment.description: Inline documentation key ($comment, $comment_specialization, …). Ignored by the toolkit; permitted so the annotated template validates.
